turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is... I just feel like I’m constantly running on a motor lately. It's like I finish one thing, whether it's at school or at home, and I immediately jump right into the next thing. I just never seem to be able to shut myself off.

symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient explicitly describes feeling like they are constantly running on a motor and unable to shut themselves off between activities.

turns.doctor_question: Can you tell me how far back you can remember feeling this way—did this restless, 'always on the go' feeling start when you were a child, or is it something more recent?
turns.patient_response: It goes way back. It's definitely not recent. My mother actually used to joke that even in elementary school, I basically taught the class from my seat. I was just... always out of my chair, talking, or cutting in before the teacher even finished giving directions. So, yeah, this was part of who I was long before adulthood. It's not something that just started up recently with any family changes or anything like that. It's always been this way.

symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient reports being 'always out of my chair' during elementary school classes, confirming leaving their seat when remaining seated was expected.
symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient describes 'cutting in before the teacher even finished giving directions,' indicating a pattern of interrupting others.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from feeling restless and impulsive, do you also struggle to stay focused on tasks, often losing track of details or forgetting things, like schoolwork or daily responsibilities?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I mean, I don't have trouble focusing on things. As a special education teacher, I have to keep track of a lot of details and paperwork, and I manage that just fine. I don't really forget things or lose track of what I'm supposed to be doing. It's more just... the physical restlessness, the needing to move, that's the main issue. Not my focus.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient explicitly confirms that physical restlessness and needing to move is their main issue.
symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient denies having trouble keeping track of details or paperwork.
symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly states they do not have trouble focusing on things.
symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient states they do not forget things or lose track of what they are supposed to be doing.

turns.doctor_question: Does this constant need to be moving or jumping into things cause problems for you in more than one area of your life—for example, both at work and at home or in relationships—or is it mostly noticeable in just one setting?
turns.patient_response:
It's definitely causing problems in multiple areas. It's not just at school. At work, the complaints have actually gotten serious enough that they recently put me on a corrective plan. And at home... well, my spouse says our caregiving routines are a lot harder now because they feel like they have to manage my energy on top of everything else we have going on. 

It's tough. I really feel like I’m damaging trust with my colleagues and my family, which is frustrating because, in my mind, I’m honestly just trying to help. But it just ends up being too much for everyone to deal with.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often find yourself interrupting others, blurting out answers, or having trouble waiting your turn, in addition to the physical restlessness you've described?
turns.patient_response: Yes, that happens a lot. I keep jumping into conversations... whether it's between my colleagues, or parents at school, or even my spouse and the relative we're caring for. I honestly do it because I think I'm helping or adding something useful, but I just end up talking over them. I tend to take charge of the conversation before they've even had a chance to finish what they were saying. It's a real problem.

symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient confirms frequently jumping into conversations, talking over others, and taking charge before people can finish speaking.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever gone through distinct periods—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, or had racing thoughts, that were different from your usual baseline?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't experienced anything like that. My energy level is pretty much a constant thing—it doesn't come and go in phases or distinct periods. I don't get euphoric, and my sleep is fairly normal. It's just this constant physical restlessness and impulsivity that I deal with every day.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient explicitly confirms dealing with 'constant physical restlessness' every day.
symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient denies having distinct periods of feeling elevated, euphoric, or irritable, stating they do not get euphoric.
symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient reports their sleep is 'fairly normal', denying a decreased need for sleep.
symptom_reasoning.S038: The patient responds 'No, I haven't experienced anything like that' to the doctor's question asking about racing thoughts.

turns.doctor_question: Do you also experience frequent worry, nervousness, or a sense of dread that accompanies this restlessness, or does the need to keep moving happen even when you're not feeling anxious?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't really get that sense of dread or worry. I mean, I'm not an anxious person. The moving around... it just happens all the time, even when I'm perfectly calm or in a good mood. It's not driven by nervousness at all. I just always feel like I need to be doing something.

symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient describes moving around all the time and feeling like they constantly need to be doing something, characteristic of being on the go or driven by a motor.
symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies anxiety, stating they do not experience dread or worry and are not an anxious person.
